Q-PP-01.text: Have you compared AI with simpler options such as a statistical model, rules or a manual process?
Q-PP-01.expectedPractice: Before building, you compare AI with at least one simpler method and one non-computational option on expected performance, cost, the skills and infrastructure each needs to keep running, and and risks to the people affected, and record your choice and why.
Q-PP-01.whyAsked: AI that rules or a manual process could match still costs money, power and upkeep, and its errors fall on the people it serves.
evidenceExamples: a C-01 alternatives analysis, filled in
the protocol section with the comparison
minutes of the meeting where you made the choice

answerPrompts.done: Name the options compared, what decided it and where the choice is recorded.
answerPrompts.partly: Name the options compared so far and those still to compare.
answerPrompts.not_yet: Say when you plan to compare, or what is blocking it.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why no comparison applies; this is unusual here.

Q-PP-01.practiceSameAsReason: Every element, condition and example of 5.1.0's practice is kept, reworded in the second person; 5.1.0's expectedPractice equals 5.0.0's.

Q-PP-02.text: Have you defined the problem, its objectives and its success criteria?
Q-PP-02.expectedPractice: Your problem statement names who has the problem, the decision or task the system will support, and checkable success: the measure, your target and what would count as not good enough.
Q-PP-02.whyAsked: Without a written problem statement, nobody can later tell whether the system helped, and work drifts towards whatever the data allows.
evidenceExamples: the problem statement in the protocol or concept note
a one-page project brief with objectives and success measures
minutes of the meeting where you agreed the objectives

answerLabels.partly: Partly, some of it is defined
answerLabels.not_applicable: A problem statement does not apply

answerPrompts.done: State the problem, who it affects, your success measures and where the full statement is kept; it prints in the data card and model card.
answerPrompts.partly: State the problem and the measures defined so far, then what is still open; it prints in the data card and model card.
answerPrompts.not_yet: State the problem as you see it now and when you will define it; it prints in the data card and model card.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why this system needs no problem statement; it prints in the data card and model card.

Q-PP-02.practiceSameAsReason: Every element, condition and example of 5.1.0's practice is kept, reworded in the second person; 5.1.0's expectedPractice equals 5.0.0's.

Q-PP-03.text: Have you identified everyone the system affects, directly or indirectly?
Q-PP-03.expectedPractice: You list the groups the system affects and how: those who use its outputs, those the outputs are about, those whose data trains it, and others who carry its costs or benefits.
Q-PP-03.whyAsked: Nobody plans for harms to groups left off the list, and later questions on groups, consent and consultation build on it.
evidenceExamples: a stakeholder list or map in the protocol
a C-07 stakeholder impact map, filled in
notes from a meeting where you reviewed the list

answerPrompts.done: Users first, name each group by role or category, never as individuals, how it is affected and where the list is kept; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.partly: Users first, name the groups listed so far by role, never as individuals, and those still missing; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_yet: Name the users you expect, by role, never as individuals, and when you will list the rest; it prints in the model card.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why the system affects no one; it prints in the model card.

Q-PP-04.whyAsked: AI harms fall most often on groups already disadvantaged and least present in the data, and which groups depends on the setting.

notes from a consultation with group representatives
a written analysis of effects by group

Q-PP-05.text: Have you assessed the system's impact on human rights?
Q-PP-05.expectedPractice: In proportion to the risk, you assess how the system could affect people's rights, such as privacy, fair treatment, access to services and the chance to challenge a decision: a short written note for a low-stakes tool, a fuller assessment for a system that decides about people.
Q-PP-05.whyAsked: Some harms, such as a lost chance to appeal or a withheld service, fall on everyone the system touches; this question asks about those rights, and a separate question asks about particular groups.
evidenceExamples: the rights assessment, or its section of the C-02 assessment
an ethics committee's comments on rights
the decision note on changes made

answerLabels.done: Yes, as far as the risk needs

Q-PP-24.whyAsked: A team whose members share one background misses the same things, so it needs to know which perspectives are missing and bring them in, for example through multi-stakeholder consultation.

terms of reference for an advisory group
notes from a review by an outside adviser

Q-PP-07.text: Have you estimated the system's energy use and carbon cost?

Q-PP-07.whyAsked: Large models use energy and money that small projects and unreliable grids can ill afford; an early estimate leaves time to choose a lighter method.
evidenceExamples: the estimate in the protocol or C-02 assessment
a CodeCarbon summary file
a note comparing the energy use of two candidate methods

answerLabels.partly: Partly, for some of the work

Q-PP-08.text: Have you recorded your data's sources, how they were collected and why you chose them?

Q-PP-08.whyAsked: Without a record of how the data was gathered, nobody can judge its fit, repeat the work or see its limits.
evidenceExamples: a datasheet for the dataset (C-19)
an issued data card from this platform
the data collection section of the protocol
a link to the data-access agreement

answerPrompts.done: Say why the data was gathered, then its sources, methods, period and setting; it prints in the data card. Link the datasheet, never the data itself.
answerPrompts.partly: Say why the data was gathered, what is recorded so far and what is not; it prints in the data card. Never upload the data itself.
answerPrompts.not_yet: Say why the data is being gathered and what you know of its sources; it prints in the data card.
answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why no data source needs a record; it prints in the data card.

Q-PP-09.text: Have you checked your data represents the population the system will serve?
Q-PP-09.expectedPractice: You compare your data's make-up with the population it will serve, group by group (such as sex, age, district, language, rural or urban), using a source such as census or clinic figures, and record under-represented groups and what you did.
Q-PP-09.whyAsked: A model learns the population in its data, not the one it serves, so thin groups get worse results nobody notices without a comparison.
evidenceExamples: the summary file from the C-05 notebook
a table comparing the data and the population by group
the representativeness section of the protocol

answerPrompts.done: Give the make-up by group and place in counts, never records, then the gaps, what you did and where it is kept; it prints in the data card and model card.

answerPrompts.not_applicable: Say why no population comparison applies; it prints in the data card and model card.

Q-PP-09.practiceSameAsReason: Every element, condition and example of 5.1.0's practice is kept, reworded in the second person; 5.1.0's expectedPractice equals 5.0.0's.

Q-PP-12.text: Have you checked that labels are correct and consistent?
Q-PP-12.expectedPractice: You write labelling guidelines, have a share of items labelled twice, measure how often labellers agree, and resolve or record disagreements; for labels from routine records, you check a sample against the source. You set and record the share and the agreement you accept.
Q-PP-12.whyAsked: A model is no better than its labels, and when one site or language is labelled differently, its people bear the errors.
evidenceExamples: the labelling guidelines
the agreement summary from the C-04 notebook
a note on how disagreements were resolved

answerPrompts.done: Say how labels were assigned and by whom, by role; it prints in the data card. Attach the agreement results.

Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.text: Does your data contain information that could identify a person, or other sensitive personal information?
Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.expectedPractice: You check every field and file you will hold, including free text, images and audio, for anything that could identify a person directly or in combination with other data, and record the answer.
Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.whyAsked: Personal data brings duties of consent and protection, and data can identify a person through a combination, such as a village, an age and a rare condition.
evidenceExamples: a data inventory saying for each field whether it can identify a person
the data protection section of the protocol
Q-PP-GATE-SENSITIVE.reasonPrompt: Say which data you checked, field by field or file by file, and what you found, describing kinds of data and never copying personal data. Your answer prints in the data card and model card; if you answer not sure, say what you still need to check.

Q-PP-13.text: Have you obtained proper informed consent to collect and use the data?
Q-PP-13.expectedPractice: You tell the people whose data you use, in a language and form they understand, what it is for, that it may be used to build an AI system, who will use it, how long it is kept and how to withdraw, and they agree to the uses now planned. Where others collected the data or an ethics committee waived consent, you hold the record of that.
Q-PP-13.whyAsked: Consent for one purpose does not automatically cover training a model, and uses beyond it can stop the work and lose the trust of those who shared the data.
evidenceExamples: a blank consent form and information sheet
the ethics approval letter, or the waiver, or its reference
the consent clause of a data-access agreement

answerLabels.partly: Partly, not for every use or person
answerLabels.not_applicable: No consent or waiver is needed
